reasons: Deviation classification is correct: p0281 imposes a flat mutual prior-written-approval requirement on assignment with no affiliate/M&A carve-out for IBM (Customer) and no reasonableness standard on the consent IBM must obtain, so it fails the fallback (successor assignment on notice plus consent not unreasonably withheld) and sits in walk-away territory under the rule.

Redline reaches the preferred position with the operative minimum: it preserves the existing mutual consent sentence (adding only the playbook's reasonableness standard), adds the affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice for IBM, and leaves MSL's Related Company consent and residual restrictions/subcontracting duties untouched.

The 0.807 changed-character ratio is explained by the necessarily inserted carve-out sentence rather than gratuitous rewriting; substance of the original clause is retained, so the advisory check does not warrant failure.

Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, concise and cites the playbook position; the added confirmation that a change of control gives MSL no termination/suspension/re-pricing right is consistent with the redline guidance and is a minor belt-and-braces addition, not an over-reach, given Section 16.5 binds only MSL.
No double-flagging or direction error: the edit benefits Customer and the added reasonableness qualifier on the general consent sentence mirrors the rule's own preferred wording.
